### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a5ddeb6ead111f4d1a7373e05cf5ddcbab2b86a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：没有。只是把一组权限测试拆小，避免 CI 忙的时候超时。
- 为什么做：这组测试在 CI 高负载时会超时，让无关的 PR 一直是红的。
- 出错会怎样：只影响测试，产品代码不变。撤回即可。
- 要你做什么：无。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `3de047739a` · 2026-11-19T09:59Z
- **Shape:** test-only, 1 file (`plugin-security/src/org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts`), +19/−16, no changeset because nothing publishes. Not governed. K = 6 since base `a9b36eff`, and it merges cleanly into current main.
- **Fixes vs card (#35436: "fix the time budget, not the assertions"; split the per-variant loop or declare a measured budget; don't raise the global `testTimeout`, skip or delete anything):**
  - The `AUDITOR_VARIANTS` loop moves outside `it`, so 12 cases (posture × caller) become 36 (posture × caller × variant).
  - Every `expect` line is unchanged, and `cell` still names caller · variant. Each case seeds its own holdings (`seedAuditorHolding` with variant-prefixed ids) and runs the same `finally` cleanup over the four holders.
  - There is no timeout raise, skip or deletion. The `test-budget: 20` header keeps its figure and class, and its REASON now counts 128 cases (104 + 24) and says why the split happened. The dev reads that the header governs the per-file report line, not vitest's 5 s per-case default, which is why splitting was the route.
- **One semantic note, acceptable:** cleanup now runs after each variant, where it used to run once after all three. So variants 2 and 3 no longer start with variant 1's leftover inserted row. Each variant's assertions read only its own set or position and its own ids, and the verdict table is unchanged, so the pins are, if anything, better isolated.
- **Measurement:** locally the slowest case drops from 611 ms to 223 ms (×0.36). Applied to the card's worst CI reading of 5534 ms, that is about 2.0 s, under the 5 s default with headroom.
- **Gates:** on `3de04773`, 12 success and 24 skipped, with 0 failed and 23 still running at review. data-1 lands only on full green, and a red that is not the timeout comes back here.
- **Landing clause:** not governed, so data-1 lands it with no L2 owed (test-only, no contract face). Then data-1 merges main into #35386. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.
